note: Recovered round: the workflow died after the builders and integrator finished, and the stall daemon died with it — unnoticed for 11.7 hours, because the heartbeat file existed but nothing read it. Fixed: stallcheck now alarms on its own watch's staleness, proven by backdating the heartbeat. The critique was relaunched separately so no builder work was re-spent. Scores are plateauing (mean delta +2.4 against round 3's +10, nothing across 60) and the critics found why — THE MEASUREMENT LAYER IS NOW THE PROBLEM. The materials critic showed the previous verdict's headline 49.3% was not reproducible because the ellipse mask was refit per round (with a fixed mask r4 was 33.6%), and that the builder's own probe keyed on G<0.80R, which by construction cannot see a white foam pip — the exact defect it was meant to measure. It returned 4.89% and let the target look met. Builders are optimising against instruments that cannot see the failure, and deltas between rounds are not real.

pieces.name: Juice fluid
pieces.biggestGap: The r4 gap did not close: every resolvable droplet is still ONE convex analytic primitive — in the 12-60 px band 58.9% of our blobs fit a mathematically perfect ellipse to within 10% IoU (r4: 58.5%) against plate-01's 22.7%, and full convexity got WORSE (solidity>=0.95 on 28.0% of blobs, up from r4's 16.4%, against the plate's 10.3%) — because the new outline harmonic is a star-convex radial dent that can never produce a neck, a satellite or a pinched doublet, and it is multiplied to literally zero by defocus.
